name: metview
why: ECMWF's meteorological workstation lets you actually work with weather data at home, a real science tool, though heavy and niche.

brief.what_it_is: Metview is a meteorological workstation application from ECMWF, developed with INPE (Brazil's National Institute for Space Research). Per its homepage, it covers data access, processing and visualisation for operational and research meteorologists. It has an icon-based graphical interface for interactive work and a Python interface for batch processing. Its installation page says the core binaries contain the GUI, most of the data processing code and the Macro programming language, and that the Python bindings sit on top of those binaries. The input is meteorological data, which the docs describe as reachable through MARS requests, and the output is processed data and plots, which can be saved as PNG, PDF or SVG files or shown inline in Jupyter notebooks.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes Metview as "a complete working environment" for both operational and research meteorologists, combining data access, processing and visualisation in one tool.
brief.how_it_works: The core 'binaries' hold the user interface, most of the data processing code and the Macro language, and they can run standalone. The Python bindings are a separate install that calls into those binaries, and on import they run the Metview startup script to set up the working environment, with an 8-second default timeout that can be raised through an environment variable.

brief.install_notes: Binaries and Python bindings are installed separately, and the bindings need the binaries. The docs recommend a conda environment (conda create --name myenv, conda activate myenv, then install metview and metview-python from conda-forge). Virtualenv users must install the binaries another way, for example with Homebrew, then pip install metview. Metview's Python bindings are also on GitHub at ecmwf/metview-python. Optional environment variables include METVIEW_PYTHON_DEBUG=1 for extra debugging and METVIEW_MARS_LOG=1 for more MARS request output. I did not see account or licence requirements on the pages I read, but I did not open the Licence page.
brief.standout: It has two front ends on one core: a graphical icon-based workstation and a Python API for batch work, with a Macro language also in the binaries. Pre-built packages from ECMWF itself are published on both Homebrew and conda, and a no-GUI batch build exists for notebook environments.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The docs say the brew and conda packages are maintained by ECMWF and are generally up to date. I did not find a release date or last-commit date on the pages I read, so recency is unverified.
brief.caveats: Homebrew on Linux is noted as untested. The Ubuntu apt packages are community-built and not maintained by ECMWF. The Python bindings cannot run without the binaries. The scout note describes it as heavy and niche, and the docs describe a full workstation with a GUI. The docs do not mention installation size or system requirements in the pages I read. The licence was not checked.
quotes: Metview is a meteorological workstation application designed to be a complete working environment for both the operational and research meteorologist.
It features both a powerful icon-based user interface for interactive work and a Python interface for batch processing.
The brew and conda packages are maintained by ECMWF and are generally up to date.
